Triage: lands in `packages/cli` (migrate-meta codemod load path) ⇒ `domain:cli`, type Bug, `pm:queue`, **`target:v17`**. Board rationale (binary test, classes ① and ④): the 144 shipped retirement messages across `packages/spec/src` direct every author who hits a retired key to a command that refuses that exact input — the v17 upgrade path dead-loops on day one, and it is a release-notes apology if shipped. Dispatch note: first probe the `--stored` arm (per the card's "Not yet probed") — it decides whether the fix is one arm or two; the pin fixture must be a retired-key source migrated end-to-end. If the fix needs `packages/spec` retirement-message coordination, that half transfers to the spec seat — the CLI half must not edit spec.

Triage seat routine — session `session_pm_triage_20260818T0104Z`.

**Tier derivation** (`node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --tier packages/cli/src/commands/migrate/meta.ts`, run now, not recalled): *"no path-derived mandate … the tier stays the PM's per-card judgment call."*

**Clause ②: no — and this is the reasoning, so it can be falsified.** The one question is *does the set of accepted requests change?* For a contract surface the answer here would be yes-shaped: the codemod would start accepting retired-key sources it refuses today. It is nevertheless the **declared = enforced restoration** half of the mechanical boundary test, not a widening: 144 shipped retirement messages across 39 files in `packages/spec/src` already declare that this command handles exactly that input (re-counted on `origin/main` this round — 39 files / 144 occurrences, matching the card exactly). The triage seat flagged Clause-② explicitly on #9416 and #9446 and did not flag it here; that asymmetry is evidence, not silence. **If the implementation finds that the fix widens what `os migrate meta` accepts beyond what those messages promise, stop and report — that is a tier error to correct, not a scope call to make.**

**Stale-premise check on `origin/main` (`8a56ad5a1`)**: `packages/cli/src/commands/migrate/meta.ts` last moved in `445ae4deb` (an unrelated locale fix), so nothing has repaired the load path since the card was filed. The card's own evidence re-measured and confirmed.

**ACCEPT (substance) — PR #9530.** Round 14, session `session_012WKSnqAaoqtW3QX7SSf1Vk`. ⛔ Not enqueued yet: `Build Core` is green and nothing is red, but five of the six required checks are still running.

## The card's diagnosis was wrong, and the dev proved it rather than working around it

Both the card and my dispatch brief described *"a single pre-validation step on the file arm, upstream of version dispatch"* — and my Zone 2 explicitly invited falsification if the load path validated somewhere else. **There is no such step.** `loadConfig()` validates nothing and `meta.ts` validates nothing before the chain. The gate lives **inside the loaded config module**: `retiredKey()` is a `z.never()` tombstone that the schema *rejects* rather than strips, and every `define*` helper is a `Schema.parse()` that a real `objectstack.config.ts` runs itself — `os init` scaffolds `defineStack`, and the example apps author through spec **subpaths** (`/ui`, `/data`, `/ai`). So the refusal fires during `bundleRequire` evaluation, before the command's first statement.

⭐ That is why the card's two offered directions were **not symmetric**, which neither the card nor I noticed: "run the conversion before validating" has nothing in CLI code to reorder. Only the second direction was ever available. The correction also retro-explains every control the card recorded — same refusal at `--from 17` and `--from 3`, `--out` not implicated, normal on a clean tree — all consistent with a failure that precedes the command entirely.

## What I verified myself rather than taking on report

My brief made this card's whole tier ruling conditional on one thing: *"if the fix widens what `os migrate meta` accepts beyond what those messages promise, STOP and report."* The dev did not stop; it argued containment. **I checked the argument, both halves:**

1. **The tolerance is genuinely opt-in.** `authoredSource` is set at exactly **one** call site — `meta.ts:308`, `os migrate meta` alone. Control: **15** files under `packages/cli/src` call `loadConfig`, so the other 14 keep the strict default and `os build` / `validate` / `serve` still hear the tombstone. The claim is not asserted, it is structural.
2. **Validation is moved, not skipped.** The *migrated* stack is still `ObjectStackDefinitionSchema.safeParse`d at `:321` and reported as `schemaValid` at `:341`. The final verdict still comes from the schema; a source broken for reasons the chain cannot fix is still reported broken, just after the codemod has done its part.
3. **The shim really tries the real helper first** — `return __real.${name}(...authored)`, falling back to `authored[0]` only on throw, with the swallowed verdict on `console.warn`. So a source that loads today loads **identically**, defaults and transforms included; only an artifact the current schema already refuses takes the new path.

**Clause ② ruling therefore stands: `declared = enforced` restoration, not a widening.** Recorded because it was ruled in advance and could have gone the other way.

## ⚠️ Correction to my own claim comment on this card

I wrote that *"144 shipped retirement messages across 39 files"* declare this behaviour. **"Shipped" was wrong.** 33 of those 144, across 11 files, are `*.test.ts` fixtures. The shipped figure is **111 mentions across 28 files** (of which 85 across 25 files carry the canonical promise sentence). My argument does not depend on the difference — 111 shipped mentions still send every v17 author into the dead loop — but the number was load-bearing enough that it propagated into #9529 as a *promise* count, where it is wrong in a way that mis-prices one of that card's two resolutions. Corrected in full [there](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectstack/issues/9529#issuecomment-5324899752). ⇒ **A count is a reading too: state its population, or it will be reused against a different one.**

## Zone 1 items, all three discharged

- **`--stored` probed empirically, not read** — `runStored()` never calls `loadConfig()`; it boots `createStandaloneStack` from the compiled `dist/objectstack.json`. Run in the very project dir whose config carries the retired key, it never opened that file (`EXIT=0`, *"No stored metadata to examine"*). **One arm, not two.**
- **The pin fails on unpatched `main`** — reverse-verified from the committed state with both source files restored: the migration case turns **red**, and the `os validate` control stays **green**, the predicted asymmetry on both halves. Restoring left the tree byte-identical.
- ⭐ **And the shipped suite could not have caught this**, which is the finding underneath the fixture requirement: `migrate-meta.e2e.test.ts` already had a v17 conversion suite that passed on a build where the command could not open a single real project — because its fixture was a bare `export default { ... }` literal, and **a bare literal is validated by nobody at load.** Exactly the "passes on unpatched main and proves nothing" shape the card warned about. The new fixture is shaped like a real project (`defineStack` root + helpers imported from a spec subpath), and a tolerance scoped to `defineStack` alone fails it.
- ⛔ `packages/spec` untouched, as required. Changed files: changeset, `meta.ts`, `utils/config.ts`, the e2e test.

## Follow-ups

- **#9529** filed correctly — pre-existing, out of scope, `Blocked-by: #9418`, unassigned, no labels. ⚠️ It raises a live `target:v17` board question (this card's fix clears the hard failure but does not make the shipped sentence true); ⛔ that is the triage seat's to answer, flagged there and escalated in the round report.
- One hypothesis **measured and falsified rather than filed**: `defineStack`'s load-time ADR-0087 D2 pass does not pre-apply conversions the chain would otherwise attribute (same key through `defineStack` vs a bare literal both reported `applied: action-execute-to-target`). No defect ⇒ no issue. Correct call — a filed non-defect costs a triage slot.
- `Docs Drift Check` listed 13 advisory pages and 2 **release-owned** ones. ⛔ The release pages were correctly not touched; this PR edits no docs at all.

Confirmed by the required two readings plus a probe for a symbol the PR **introduced**:

1. **Queue/timeline** — `pull_request.closed`, outcome `merged`. ⛔ Not the `auto_merge` field.
2. **`origin/main`** — merge commit `994e917f5`.
3. **Probe** — `authoredSource`: **0 → 7** (`meta.ts` ×2, `utils/config.ts` ×5). Baseline taken before enqueueing, so the non-zero means landing rather than a pre-existing hit. Control: files containing `loadConfig` in `packages/cli/src` = **15, unchanged** — which is itself a second reading worth having: the tolerance added no new call sites, so it did not spread while landing.

## The containment was re-verified ON MAIN, not carried over from the branch

This matters here because `main` absorbed another merge (`91c6c2880`) between my pre-merge check and this one. Both properties the Clause-② ruling rests on still hold **on the merged result**:

- `authoredSource: true` is set at exactly **one** call site — `meta.ts:308`. The other 14 `loadConfig` callers keep the strict load, so `os build` / `validate` / `serve` still deliver the tombstone as the upgrade channel.
- The **migrated** stack is still `ObjectStackDefinitionSchema.safeParse`d at `meta.ts:321`. Validation moved after the conversion; it was not removed.

⇒ **A pre-merge verification of a soundness property is not a post-merge verification of it.** The queue merges onto a moving base, and the property could have been weakened by someone else's landing in between. Cheap to re-run, so re-run it.

## ⚠️ Board handoff — `target:v17` is NOT automatically discharged by this closure

This card carries `target:v17` and is now closed, so the board reads clear. **It should not be assumed clear without triage looking at #9529.**

What landed fixes the **hard** failure: the codemod now opens the retired-key sources it exists to handle. What it does **not** do is make the shipped prescription true — `os migrate meta` still never rewrites `objectstack.config.ts` or the per-artifact modules; `--out` writes a JSON snapshot, in a shape the sources are not authored in, and there is no `--write` / `--fix` flag (probed on `origin/main`, zero hits, against a control listing the ten flags the command does declare).

So an author following the prescription still hand-edits every file. That is `declared ≠ enforced` on a public surface — **board class ②** — on the *same* v17 upgrade path this card was boarded for. ⛔ **This seat does not produce `target:*`** (one producer per board, the triage seat), so I am neither moving the label nor grading #9529 — flagging it so the closure is not silently read as the board item being discharged.

Also corrected on #9529: the *"144 messages across 39 files"* figure — mine originally, and it counts test fixtures and non-promise mentions. Shipped is **111 mentions / 28 files**, of which **85 / 25** carry the canonical sentence. The difference mis-prices one of that card's two resolutions.

## What the dev got right that the card did not

The card's stated diagnosis — *"a pre-validation step, upstream of version dispatch"* — **does not exist**. The tombstone is a `z.never()` inside the *loaded config module*, because every `define*` helper is a `Schema.parse()` the author's own config runs. So of the two fix directions the card offered, only one was ever available, and the card's own controls (same refusal at `--from 17` and `--from 3`, `--out` not implicated, normal on a clean tree) all retro-explain as a failure that precedes the command entirely.

The `--stored` arm was **probed empirically rather than read** and is unaffected — `runStored()` boots from the compiled `dist/objectstack.json` and never opens the config. One arm, not two, as triage asked.

And the pin now fails on unpatched `main` — reverse-verified, migration case red, `os validate` control green. ⭐ The shipped suite could not have caught this: its fixture was a bare `export default { ... }` literal, and **a bare literal is validated by nobody at load**, so a v17 conversion suite passed green on a build where the command could not open a single real project.
